landing.heroTitle: AI teams that run your work
landing.heroTagline: Toone turns businesses into AI-native companies. It captures how your organization works, including its processes, knowledge and tools, then operates all of it with a swarm of AI agents under human governance.
landing.pillarsSub: Seven things become true once your organization runs on Toone.
landing.p1d: Playbooks that run themselves as routines, sub-routines and schedules. Crafting one is deterministic work, much like wiring an n8n flow, except you write it in natural language. Every run stays debuggable, with agents diagnosing how it is going while it happens.
landing.p2d: An organizational knowledge graph that outlives every chat and every employee.
landing.p3d: They hold roles in departments, keep schedules, produce artefacts, and escalate to a human when it matters.
landing.p4d: Routines are written to delegate. Work moves between departments in clean compartments, so every agent holds a narrow remit and the whole organization behaves like one body.
landing.p5d: Your external tools are mapped as replayable workflows and treated as first-class integrations, scoped to what your company actually needs. Anything missing gets built custom.
landing.p6d: Gates, approvals, drafts-only outbound and redaction. Autonomy inside the boundaries you set, with accountability for every action an agent takes.
landing.p7d: Recommended templates, MCP tools, processes and integrations, assembled for your use case. Today that covers software engineering, SEO and growth, outreach and support, product strategy, science and research, and headquarters.

cases.name: Truleaf.org
cases.lede: Truleaf turns published science into decision-ready evidence for teams developing pesticide-free crop protection. That work traditionally costs a research team four to eight weeks of manual literature review per agent. Its research pipeline, its go-to-market and its engineering all run as Toone organizations, and it becomes the first white-label deployment: the same engine, their brand, their domain.

blocks.d: Literature ingestion, performance extraction across strains and conditions, contradiction resolution, regulatory-readiness scoring, and a provenance audit that locks every claim to its original source. Weeks of manual review become hours.

A competitor radar walks named competitors' sites, changelogs and pricing every week. Market trends, customer voice and review mining all feed one evidence gate, where a bet advances only once its evidence is recorded in the knowledge graph.
Daily rank tracking through mapped analytics sessions, query mining, cannibalization and index-bloat audits, and a content pipeline that runs from brief intake through to a publish-readiness check.
Bug triage, review queue and release readiness run on cadence. Architecture-drift scans, dependency hygiene, dead-code sweeps and a debt register keep the codebase healthy between releases.

cases.name: micoo
cases.lede: micoo is the reference case for the transformation motion: a working business encoded into templates and routines. Its engineering organization now runs itself from intake through to the delivery brief, and its people spend their time on decisions.

blocks.d: A daily brief covers the delta across every in-flight item: what moved, what is blocked and on whom, and where reality drifted from the plan. Blockers escalate to the departments that own them. If nothing moved, the brief says so in three lines.
Incoming work is triaged, planned and broken into sub-routines automatically, then checked against an explicit definition of done before anything gets called finished.
Architecture-drift scans, dependency hygiene, consistency audits and dead-code sweeps run on a schedule. This is the maintenance work every team intends to do and never gets to.

A tech radar watches releases, deprecations and security advisories. The research department turns those raw signals into evaluated positions and spike proposals, so technology choices arrive early enough to be decisions.

faq.title: Perguntas, respondidas.
faq.sub: A versão curta de tudo o que nos perguntam.
faq.a1: Um app para macOS que opera uma organização de agentes de IA para a sua empresa — departamentos, agentes com papéis e rotinas agendadas, sobre um grafo de conhecimento da empresa.
faq.q2: Qual a diferença para um chatbot?
faq.a2: Um chatbot responde quando você pergunta. Os agentes do Toone têm papéis, seguem rotinas agendadas, compartilham memória pelo grafo e passam trabalho entre si — o resultado chega sem você pedir.
faq.a3: Trabalhos recorrentes — resumos, pipelines de conteúdo, monitoramento, pesquisa — definidos em arquivos simples que os agentes executam no cronograma, com artefatos auditáveis.
faq.a4: Não. As organizações partem de templates e as rotinas são arquivos em linguagem natural. Quem é técnico pode inspecionar tudo no nível de arquivo.
faq.a5: No seu Mac. Sua organização é uma pasta de arquivos legíveis e os agentes rodam localmente — apenas as chamadas ao modelo saem da máquina.
faq.q6: Quais modelos de IA ele usa?
faq.a6: A família Claude da Anthropic, via Claude Code. Cada conversa pode fixar o próprio modelo.
faq.a7: O app desktop é para macOS hoje, por download direto. Mais plataformas estão no roadmap.
faq.a8: O Toone é gratuito durante o acesso antecipado. Os agentes usam a sua própria assinatura da Anthropic.
faq.q9: Pode rodar com a marca da minha empresa?
faq.a9: Sim — o Toone é white-label: o mesmo motor com a configuração da sua marca.

statement.title: Sua empresa já sabe como funcionar.
statement.lead: O conhecimento já está lá — em arquivos, ferramentas e cabeças. O Toone dá estrutura a ele: um grafo vivo do que sua empresa sabe e uma organização de agentes de IA que o coloca para trabalhar no cronograma.
